ety.text: From Latin pecūliāris (“one's own”), from pecūlium (“private property”), from pecus (“cattle”).

senses.d: Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual.
ex: The sky had a peculiar appearance before the storm.
It would be rather peculiar to see a kangaroo hopping down a city street.

senses.d: Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.
One's own; belonging solely or especially to an individual; not shared or possessed by others.
ex: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
hymns […] that Christianity hath peculiar unto itself

senses.d: Particular; individual; special; appropriate.
ex: while each peculiar power forgoes his wonted seat
My fate is Juno's most peculiar care.

senses.d: That which is peculiar; a sole or exclusive property; a prerogative; a characteristic.
an ecclesiastical district, parish, chapel or church outside the jurisdiction of the bishop of the diocese in which it is situated.

grp.label: common or usual for a particular place or circumstance

senses.d: To strike or pierce with the beak or bill (of a bird).
ex: The birds pecked at their food.
And the Wicked Witch said to the King Crow, "Fly at once to the strangers; peck out their eyes and tear them to pieces."

senses.d: To form by striking with the beak or a pointed instrument.
ex: to peck a hole in a tree

senses.d: To strike, pick, thrust against, or dig into, with a pointed instrument, especially with repeated quick movements.
To seize and pick up with the beak, or as if with the beak; to bite; to eat; often with up.
ex: This fellow pecks up wit as pigeons peas.

senses.d: To do something in small, intermittent pieces.
ex: He has been pecking away at that project for some time now.

senses.d: To type by searching for each key individually.
To type in general.
To kiss briefly.
An act of striking with a beak.
A small kiss.
One quarter of a bushel; a dry measure of eight quarts; equal to approximately 9092 cubic centimeters in the imperial system or 8810 cubic centimeters in the U.S. system.
ex: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.

senses.d: Similar units in other systems of measure, such as the Roman modius or Chinese dou.
A great deal; a large or excessive quantity.
ex: She figured most children probably ate a peck of dirt before they turned ten.

senses.d: To throw.

ex: an occurrence of peck in rice

senses.d: Food.
ex: Gemmen, have you ordered the peck and booze for the evening?
